newsitem.title: UK: IPE crude oil futures close up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: IPE crude oil futures close up but off highs.

text.p: IPE crude futures closed firmer on Monday but off the day's highs after trying to test the upside in late trade but failing to break through its first resistance level, traders said. July Brent closed 12 cents up at $19.52 a barrel after hitting a high of $19.62 in the late afternoon, or one point off its first resistance level, on the back of stronger-than-expected NYMEX complex.

August Brent, which rose earlier to $19.71, closed nine cents a barrel up at $19.58. "It was not a very positive close by any means. There was only one buyer towards the close and some selling," one trader said. "We were looking for June WTI to close above $21.00, so it doesn't look too good for tomorrow," the trader added. July Brent started to climb as NYMEX's WTI traded above the $21.00 mark towards the end of Monday's session, but the later then trimmed its gains to close at $20.95 or seven cents up on Friday. July WTI hit a high of $21.17 earlier in the day. Traders said the market took notice but did not greatly react to news that U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan on Monday recommended a six-month renewal of Iraq's "oil-for-food" deal once it expires on June 7.

"It was looking like it (United Nations) was going to do the rollover, so it did not have a major impact," one trader said. "Unless there is a change in the amounts of crude we are talking about here, then I don't think it is news as such to the market," a second trader said. "If there is a change in sentiment, i.e the U.N. says that this will be the last time we work out this agreement and as of today we will allow Iraq to sell on the open market as they wish then it will have an impact, of course," he added. The current deal calls for $2 billion worth of oil sales over six months so Baghdad can buy food and medicine for its people, suffering from U.N. sanctions imposed in 1990 after Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait.
Earlier, IPE gas oil futures closed on the upside on Monday on the back of some pre-close buying, traders said.
June gas oil closed $1.50 up at $174 a tonne and July gas oil closed at $175.25 a tonne, also $1.50 higher than Friday's close.
